title: Regular expressions
test_conventions: Learner code runs first in a fresh namespace. Each test is a Python snippet (assert statements) executed afterwards in the same namespace; the learner's printed output is available to tests as the string variable __stdout__. expected_output comparisons are exact after stripping trailing whitespace on every line. No input(), network or pip. Files may be created in the working directory (an in-memory file system in the browser); use unique file names. The learner's source code is available to tests as the string variable __source__ (use it with ast or substring checks to reject hard-coded answers).

worked_example.code:
import re
txt = 'I love to teach python'
print(re.match('love', txt))
print(re.search('love', txt).span())
notes: re.match only looks at the START of the string, so it gives None here.
re.search looks anywhere and returns a match object; .span() gives (start, end).
notes_tr: re.match sadece metnin BAŞINA bakar, bu yüzden burada None verir.
re.search her yerde arar ve bir match nesnesi döndürür; .span() (başlangıç, bitiş) verir.

exercises.code:
import re
txt = 'I love to teach python and javaScript'
print(re.match('I love to teach', txt) is None)
print(re.match('teach', txt) is None)
print(re.search('teach', txt).span())
exercises.explanation: 'I love to teach' is at the beginning, so match finds it (not None -> False). 'teach' is not at the beginning, so match gives None (-> True). search finds 'teach' at positions 10 to 15.

misconceptions.True\nFalse\n(10, 15): The first pattern really is at the start; the second is not. Check which one gives None.
misconceptions.False\nFalse\n(10, 15): re.match fails when the pattern is not at the very start of the text.

exercises.explanation_tr: 'I love to teach' metnin başındadır, bu yüzden match onu bulur (None değil -> False). 'teach' başta değildir, match None verir (-> True). search 'teach'i 10 ile 15 arasında bulur.

misconceptions_tr.True\nFalse\n(10, 15): İlk desen gerçekten başta; ikincisi değil. Hangisinin None verdiğine bak.
misconceptions_tr.False\nFalse\n(10, 15): Desen metnin en başında değilse re.match başarısız olur.

import re

findall returns a list of ALL matches.
notes_tr: [Aa] A ya da a demektir; re.I büyük/küçük harfi yok sayar: ikisi de tüm 'apple'ları bulur.

exercises.code:
import re
txt = 'This example was made on December 6,  2019 and revised on July 8, 2021'
print(re.findall(r'\d', txt))
print(re.findall(r'\d+', txt))
print(re.findall(r'\d{4}', txt))
exercises.explanation: \d matches single digits (ten of them). \d+ matches runs of one or more digits: 6, 2019, 8, 2021. \d{4} accepts only runs of four digits: 2019 and 2021.

misconceptions.['6', '2019', '8', '2021']\n['6', '2019': \d alone matches ONE digit at a time, so the first list is longer.
misconceptions.['6', '2', '0', '1', '9', '8', '2', '0',: \d{4} needs exactly four digits in a row, so 6 and 8 do not match.

exercises.explanation_tr: \d tek tek rakamlarla eşleşir (toplam on tane). \d+ bir ya da daha çok rakamdan oluşan dizileri bulur: 6, 2019, 8, 2021. \d{4} yalnızca dört rakamlık dizileri alır: 2019 ve 2021.

misconceptions_tr.['6', '2019', '8', '2021']\n['6', '2019': \d tek başına bir seferde TEK rakamla eşleşir, bu yüzden ilk liste daha uzundur.
misconceptions_tr.['6', '2', '0', '1', '9', '8', '2', '0',: \d{4} art arda tam dört rakam ister, bu yüzden 6 ve 8 eşleşmez.

worked_example.code:
import re
print(re.findall(r'[Ee]-?mail', 'e-mail email Email'))
print(re.findall(r'^This', 'This is it'))
print(re.findall(r'[^A-Za-z ]+', 'on 6, 2019'))
notes: ? makes the previous part optional; ^ means the start of the text.
[^...] with the ^ INSIDE the brackets means 'not these characters'.
notes_tr: ? önceki parçayı isteğe bağlı yapar; ^ metnin başı demektir.

exercises.code:
import re
txt = 'I am not sure how to write e-mail. Some write email or E-mail or Email.'
print(re.findall(r'[Ee]-?mail', txt))
print(re.findall(r'^Some', txt))
print(re.findall(r'^I', txt))
print(re.findall(r'\.$', txt))
exercises.explanation: [Ee]-?mail finds all four spellings. ^Some finds nothing because the text starts with 'I am'. ^I matches the first letter. \.$ matches a literal dot at the very end.

misconceptions.['e-mail', 'email', 'E-mail', 'Email']\n: ^ only matches at the very START of the whole text, which begins with 'I am', not 'Some'.
The text really does start with the letter I, so ^I finds one match.

exercises.explanation_tr: [Ee]-?mail dört yazımın hepsini bulur. ^Some hiçbir şey bulmaz çünkü metin 'I am' ile başlıyor. ^I ilk harfle eşleşir. \.$ metnin en sonundaki gerçek bir noktayla eşleşir.

misconceptions_tr.['e-mail', 'email', 'E-mail', 'Email']\n: ^ yalnızca tüm metnin BAŞINDA eşleşir; metin 'Some' ile değil 'I am' ile başlıyor.
Metin gerçekten I harfiyle başlıyor, bu yüzden ^I bir eşleşme bulur.

worked_example.code:
import re
print(re.sub('%', '', 'I a%m te%acher'))
print(re.split(',', 'a,b,c'))
notes: re.sub(pattern, replacement, text) replaces every match.
re.split(pattern, text) cuts the text at every match and returns a list.
notes_tr: re.sub(desen, yerine, metin) her eşleşmeyi değiştirir.
re.split(desen, metin) metni her eşleşmede keser ve liste döndürür.

txt = 'Python python PYTHON'

hints: Compare the output with what you expect. Which words stayed?
The 4th positional parameter of re.sub is count (the number of replacements), not flags.
Pass the flag by name: ___=re.I (what is the parameter called?)

solution.approach: re.I was passed as the count argument. Pass it by name as flags=re.I.
solution.code:
import re

exercises.prompt: In your own words: what is the difference between re.match, re.search and re.findall?
exercises.prompt_tr: Kendi cümlelerinizle: re.match, re.search ve re.findall arasındaki fark nedir?
exercises.model_answer: re.match only checks the start of the text. re.search looks anywhere but returns only the first match as a match object, or None. re.findall looks everywhere and returns a list of all matches.
exercises.model_answer_tr: re.match yalnızca metnin başına bakar. re.search her yere bakar ama sadece ilk eşleşmeyi bir match nesnesi olarak (ya da None) döndürür. re.findall her yere bakar ve tüm eşleşmeleri bir liste olarak döndürür.
